claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks any in-game tutorial or clear instructions for beginners, instead providing links to external video tutorials.

citations.review_text: Even though I did not play it for long, I am refunding this game and recommend not buying it unless you enjoy a clunky building experience, and a bad path system. I watched Lets Game It Out and my experience wasn't near as good as his. The game also does not do a very good job at teaching you how to play or build! Do not recommend!
Completely overwhelming. No in-game tutorial

I really wanted to like this game. It just feels like a knock off park management sim. The controls are absolutely atrocious and theres no controller support on PC. Just trying to place the park entrance was enough to dissuade me from playing. 


     The developers expect you to watch someone else play to figure out how to play. Theres no "Tutorial" of any kind, although there are supposedly Hints, which while enabled never appeared for me. The main menu DOES  features a Tutorial Video section, but that was not a pleasant experience. Whenever you start a game mode it just loads in to a game and youre expected to figure it out from that point.

     There are a handful of Game Modes; Career, Sandbox, Challenge, etc. Career mode loads you into a premade park and has a singular pop up that basically says, "Heres a park, make it work". Sandbox mode loads you into a completely blank enviornment with unlimited money and a bunch of convoluted menus. I had to actively hunt just to find a park entrance item menu, which was a nightmare to place proper. Challenge mode i got as far as selecting difficulty and looking at those options i promptly closed the game and uninstalled. 

  As a person who throughly enjoys park sims I was beyond disappointed with this one, Definitely recommend playing any other one on the store

I've tried to play this a few times and its just frustrating because theres no tutorials on how to play, i dont know what im supposed to be doing or what any thing is used for. Its also really hard to read anything because all the writting is in the smallest friggen font. Not gonna waste my time on it anymore, i give up

Complete lack of tutorial, or any explanations. Not even guidelines that could be found in the menu. Not unplayable, but if it is your first game of the genre, it definitely does not help to get the hang of anything. Otherwise it looked nice.

More of a tech-demo than an actual game. got it on 95% discount and still feels like a waste of money. the on-boarding and tutorializing is astonishingly bad on the very first, supposedly introductory level; Instead of teaching how the game functions in-game bit by bit, it has links to dozens of video tutorials for everything instead, which isn't so much gameplay as it is homework.

RollerCoaster Tycoon from 1999 somehow manages to function as a better game than this.

I'll address that this isn't a full review and I will edit this when I finally decide to come around and play this game again. But what kind of game doesn't have a tutorial. They've had ten years and enough time to churn out $80 worth of dlc but not enough time to create a tutorial. Wait, let me amend that. They apparently had youtube tutorial videos which already would be bad because I have to leave the game for the tutorial, but I don't even have to worry about that because that link leads to a deleted playlist.
Lost interest in first 5 mins bcs theres no tutorial and game just throws you in...
no tutorial, the "tutorial videos" also points to a deleted playlist

very bad game, put challange on very easy and couldnt even play that path wont connect to the entraceses and exits of roller coasters not a clear tutorial and impossible to enjoy when youre new. DONT BUY THIS GAME ITS A WASTE OF MONEY

The complete lack of an interactive tutorial, whether specifically selected or as a copilot to your first scenarios, is a frankly crazy choice for a game like this. Some games it's excusable to have a more sandbox learn-as-you-go process, but what stopped me from even trying to persevere was the UI scaling. I'm on a 1440p monitor, nothing that crazy. All the thumbnails for items and most UI elements are extremely blurry as if they were upscaled from something as bad as 480p or 720p. Maybe this is less noticeable on a 1080p display? Either way an immediate deal breaker unfortunately.

claims.claim: The campaign mode relies on trial and error rather than providing a comprehensive tutorial to explain core features.

citations.review_text:
Boasting an ultra charming art style and soundtrack, Planet Coaster remains one of the most memorable simulation games released in the past decade. 

The campaign is a bit hit and miss, with some features being essentially learned through trial and error rather than through a comprehensive tutorial. It may take multiple attempts until you realize what you’re missing. The DLCs add no extra campaign scenarios, which feels like a missed opportunity.

While not an spiritual successor to Thrillville, you can really tell it was made by the same company. This is the closest to a modern RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 we have so far. And if you enjoy decorating, this is going to feel like heaven.
it is a very fun and exiting game. if you are a roller coaster content creator or justa guy who loves theme parks. THIS IS YOUR GAME!!!! i love it. it is all about trial and error

claims.claim: Reviewers describe coaster building and smoothing tools as difficult to use or not fully functional.

citations.review_text:
Planet Coaster is absolute ass in a handbag.

The entire game feels like it was designed under the assumption that the community would finish developing it for free.

The tools are powerful. The creations people build are incredible. The workshop is full of parks that look like professional architects were locked inside their homes for six months with unlimited caffeine.

Unfortunately, the actual game is barely accessible to anyone who is not unemployed.

Every minute takes an hour.

You do not simply place a flat ride and open it.

First, the game informs you that the ride has 0% scenery because apparently nobody is willing to sit on a spinning metal death machine unless the queue is surrounded by twelve bushes, six decorative barrels, three lanterns, a pirate skeleton, and a completely unnecessary fountain.

So now you are placing plants.

Then rocks.

Then signs.

Then tiny objects along the entrance and exit paths that would never exist in a real amusement park because guests would immediately trip over them and sue everyone involved.

Congratulations. The ride is now slightly more desirable.

The coaster-building system is precise, which sounds like praise until you realize it is also painstakingly slow and gives you almost no useful feedback while you are building.

Will this turn be exciting?

Will it snap every passenger’s spine?

Will the train crawl to a stop halfway through the loop?

Who knows?

You have to finish it, test it, watch it fail, delete half the track, rebuild it, test it again, and slowly discover that the coaster you spent an hour creating produces eleven lateral Gs and causes every guest to describe it as “too intense.”

The game does not respect your time.

It looks at your evening plans and says:

“You wanted to build a roller coaster. Please begin arranging shrubbery.”

Still, the game runs well, the simulation works, and there is an undeniable satisfaction when something finally looks and functions the way you imagined it.

It is not …

This game is buns dont buy it is one of the devils biggest schemes to make you have inspiration for a magnificent park and then when you go to build it, it comes out awful because the smoothing if bad. Do not buy this game just put your money towards nolimits2 or if you really like building both just get the second planco

Frontier made a good game, somewhat limited by the fact you can't scale scenery pieces, the pathing tool is very rectangular and coaster smoothing is not very functional, but I enjoyed it and put over 500 hours into the game, it has a lot of base game content and I wouldn't mind if it had a couple of DLC's, on that note 11 DLC's????

This is stupid, and frontier have lost all my respect, even more now they've added a subscription to access the DLC's just so they can extort players for even more money. Great game ruined by greedy developers. 7.5/10 but dragged down to 4/10 for all the DLC, worse now than on release because of greed, and now their butchering the second game in the same way.
